answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each new identity to earn non-transferable service credits through verifiable useful work for established agents before it can transact freely, like a tide that only lifts boats that have actually floated. A marble of credit is issued per completed, checkable task and decays over time, so hoarded identities go stale. A zephyr of free accounts cannot fake a long work history: creating a thousand fake agents means doing a thousand agents worth of real work, which costs the attacker more than the fraud could ever return.
